MORE THAN A PROMPT

What is a GriidAi geospatial workflow?

A GriidAi workflow is an ordered sequence that connects a spatial question to the data, GIS operations, validation checkpoints and outputs needed to answer it. For supported tasks, GriidAi can propose the implementation plan, let the user review the inputs and method, execute the approved analysis, and keep resulting layers, maps, tables or statistics available for inspection.

A workflow is more than a prompt and more than a single GIS tool. It should make the method visible enough for an expert to review what was used, what assumptions matter, what result was produced and whether the output is fit for the intended decision.

01 / THE WORKFLOW LIBRARY

Five questions. Five inspectable methods.

These are reference examples of analytical methods, not a promise of packaged one-click execution. Use your own suitable inputs, confirm available operations in the app, and review the plan and result.

Example
01 / Terrain & Hydrology

DEM Hydrology & Stream Network

How can I extract drainage patterns and a stream network from a DEM?

Turn elevation data into reviewable terrain and drainage outputs through a multi-step hydrology sequence.

INPUTSDigital elevation model + study area / AOI
Explore the example method +
  1. Inspect the DEM, CRS, elevation units, resolution and NoData.
  2. Review terrain preparation and depression handling for the study area.
  3. Use supported flow-direction and flow-accumulation operations.
  4. Apply an explicit stream-extraction threshold.
  5. Inspect intermediate layers and validate the stream network against the terrain.
Result to inspect
Flow and drainage layers, stream network, map and related analytical layers.
Validation & limits
Check grid alignment, edge effects, units, depression handling and threshold sensitivity. A derived stream network depends on the input DEM and the chosen method.

Reference example · current production verification date not published.

Example
02 / Remote Sensing & Raster

NDVI Analysis

How can I calculate and map vegetation condition from imagery?

Calculate a vegetation index from suitable red and near-infrared raster inputs, then inspect, summarize or export the result.

INPUTSCompatible red and near-infrared imagery + AOI
Explore the example method +
  1. Define the study area and relevant date or season.
  2. Inspect red and near-infrared bands, resolution, alignment and quality.
  3. Review the index calculation and missing-value treatment.
  4. Run supported raster processing and inspect the resulting NDVI layer.
  5. Review the legend, spatial patterns and any contextual summaries.
Result to inspect
NDVI raster, mapped index with legend, optional summaries where supported.
Validation & limits
Check clouds, masks, NoData and band selection. NDVI describes an index; it is not a direct crop-yield estimate or a biological diagnosis.

Reference example · current production verification date not published.

Example
03 / Network, Proximity & Coverage

Fire Station Coverage

Which areas or populations appear underserved by current fire-station coverage?

Combine facility locations with an explicit coverage method and relevant demand or population context to identify areas for deeper service review.

INPUTSStation locations + study area + demand / population context
Explore the example method +
  1. Inspect facility locations and the population or demand context.
  2. Define the service threshold and supported coverage method.
  3. Review whether the method uses straight-line distance or a supported network operation.
  4. Calculate coverage and identify gaps within the study area.
  5. Inspect affected areas and contextual summaries before drawing conclusions.
Result to inspect
Coverage/gap map and affected areas or population-context summaries where supported.
Validation & limits
A Euclidean buffer is different from travel-time coverage. Check data completeness and thresholds; this example does not guarantee emergency response times.

Reference example · current production verification date not published.

Example
04 / Climate & Coastal Risk

Sea-Level Rise

Which locations or assets are exposed under a defined sea-level-rise scenario?

Combine a defined water-level scenario with elevation and location data, then map and summarize spatial exposure under explicit assumptions.

INPUTSWater-level scenario + elevation + assets / locations + AOI
Explore the example method +
  1. Identify the scenario, source, geography and time horizon.
  2. Inspect elevation resolution, units and vertical reference.
  3. Review the exposure method and spatial assumptions.
  4. Overlay the scenario with relevant locations or assets.
  5. Inspect exposed features, mapped results and available summaries.
Result to inspect
Scenario exposure map, affected locations or areas and supporting summary table.
Validation & limits
Keep the scenario, source and elevation assumptions explicit. Exposure screening does not forecast precisely when flooding will occur or estimate damage and financial loss.

Reference example · current production verification date not published.

Example
05 / Climate & Coastal Risk

Storm Surge

Which assets or areas intersect a defined storm-surge hazard or scenario?

Use authoritative storm-surge scenario data with assets or geography to produce a reviewable coastal-exposure analysis.

INPUTSStorm-surge hazard layer + assets / population + AOI
Explore the example method +
  1. Identify the hazard source and event or scenario meaning.
  2. Inspect geography, resolution, elevation context and missing data.
  3. Review the overlay or intersection method and expected outputs.
  4. Run the supported exposure steps with the selected inputs.
  5. Inspect affected features, map and supporting statistics.
Result to inspect
Exposure map, affected features or areas and supporting statistics.
Validation & limits
Storm surge concerns storm-driven coastal flooding. It is distinct from a long-term sea-level-rise scenario; do not interchange the two or infer loss and failure probabilities.

Reference example · current production verification date not published.

See the method before the result

  1. 01

  2. 02

    Data

  3. 03

    Plan

    See the proposed inputs, method, validation and expected output.

  4. 04

    Review

    Check assumptions, units, parameters and the selected data before execution.

    Execute

    Run the approved, supported spatial operations.

  6. 06

  7. 07

AI can propose the workflow. The expert still validates the method and result.

AI proposes the work. Experts control what proceeds.

Every workflow should make its dependencies understandable.

Data with context

Identify the input layers, study area, time period and required variables. Check source rights and the actual access path.

02 / METHOD

Supported operations

A workflow combines GIS operations in an ordered method. A buffer, raster calculation or flow operation is a step, rather than the whole use case.

05 / REPEATABILITY

Keep the successful method connected to the next question.

GriidAi is designed to turn successful analytical methods into repeatable geospatial work. Continue from available session context, use trusted project data, and follow a published method where the current product supports those steps.

A reference method explains inputs, assumptions, steps and validation. It does not by itself establish a visual workflow builder, automatic version control or a one-click reusable product.

06 / READ THE EXAMPLE

What do workflow status labels mean?

Example

A reference method or demonstrated sequence. It is not necessarily packaged for one-click execution.

Beta

A publicly available workflow with stated maturity or scope limits, when specifically approved and labeled.

Live

A current workflow available for its stated use, with verified method, supported inputs and current product evidence.

The collection above currently contains Example records. No Live or Beta availability is inferred from a method description.

WORKFLOW QUESTIONS

Know what to review before you run

How can I automate a multi-step GIS workflow?+

Define the question, bring or discover relevant data, inspect the proposed plan, approve supported operations, then review maps and analytical outputs. Validate the result before exporting or continuing.

Can I use my own data?+

Supported uploaded data can become a workflow input. Inspect its structure, spatial reference, units and coverage, and choose the intended layer before reviewing the plan.

Can a workflow combine raster and vector data?+

Supported methods may combine raster and vector operations. Each input and operation still needs to be appropriate for the task; check alignment, scale and the proposed method.

Can I review a workflow before it runs?+

For supported executed tasks, the implementation plan exposes Inputs, Method, Validation and Output for user review before processing.

Can I reuse these examples?+

Use them as reference methods with suitable inputs and current supported operations. A published example does not imply that a saved, one-click workflow or a visual editor is available.

Does GriidAi replace GIS experts?+

No. Experts define the intent, review the method and validate whether the result is appropriate for its intended use.
